__baseline_prompt__.text: A fictional clinical encounter charged with dread, photographed as a grounded hospital scene. The central figure is a reference-inspired woman, preserving the supplied portrait's facial appearance and short dark bob with a light, separated fringe. She stands at the after-hours discharge records counter in a charcoal sleeveless jersey top and pale trousers, wearing a narrow hospital identification band. She has just been handed an empty transparent record sleeve. Her left hand holds its open mouth against the counter; the fingers of her right hand remain on the metal lip of the now-closed transfer hatch. Through the clear lower portion of the security glass, her thick chart rests on the staff side, close enough to see yet physically beyond her reach. The small portrait clipped to that chart repeats her face. Her eyes are fixed on this inaccessible file, her lips slightly parted and her shoulders held still; a soft amber desk lamp catches her cheek and bare forearm, giving her an intimate human presence against the building's indifferent surfaces. Immediately beyond her, a closed hospital exit door has a plainly visible steel sliding bolt across its seam. The waiting seats are empty, a queue dispenser hangs idle, and the long corridor of numbered clinical doors leads into fluorescent distance. The viewer stands beside the patient side of the counter at her eye level, close enough to understand the empty sleeve and her interrupted gesture while keeping the chart, glass barrier, and bolted exit legible in the same horizontal frame. Restrained color photography, cool green-white institutional light, one small amber pool, mild grain, real worn laminate and rubbed stainless steel. The frightening event is the hospital retaining control of her record after the ordinary promise of discharge; her living, particular presence meets a system that has stopped responding.
